task: Survey recent Lyman-alpha forest constraints on warm dark matter. How do they compare with sterile-neutrino non-resonant production? Use the sterile-nu tools for production fractions.

runs.task: Survey recent Lyman-alpha forest constraints on warm dark matter. How do they compare with sterile-neutrino non-resonant production? Use the sterile-nu tools for production fractions.

brief.summary: High-redshift Lyman-alpha forest flux power spectra are among the strongest constraints on the free-streaming of warm dark matter (WDM). The 95% CL lower limits on the thermal-relic mass have tightened over time: about 0.75 keV (Narayanan et al. 2000), 3.3 keV (Viel et al. 2013, HIRES/MIKE, z>4), 3.1 keV (Villasenor et al. 2022, 1080 Cholla simulations on Boera et al. 2019 data, with a weak likelihood peak near 4.5 keV) and 5.7 keV (Irsic et al. 2023, HIRES/UVES at z=4.2-5.0 with k_max=0.2 s/km). The Irsic et al. limit drops to 4.1 keV when restricted to k_max<0.1 s/km and earlier thermal-history priors. The dominant systematics are now IGM peculiar velocities, inhomogeneous reionization and the thermal history, rather than statistics alone. For non-resonantly produced (Dodelson-Widrow, DW) sterile neutrinos, these limits have to be converted to a sterile-neutrino mass through a transfer-function mapping. The commonly used relation from Viel et al. 2005 (astro-ph/0501562), quoted from memory and not checked against a retrieved full text, is m_s ~ 4.43 keV (m_th/keV)^{4/3} (omega_dm/0.1225)^{-1/3}. It turns 3.1-5.7 keV thermal-relic limits into roughly 20-45 keV DW limits, which are far above the masses that X-ray decay bounds allow for DW sterile neutrinos making up all of the dark matter. Pure DW production is therefore excluded as 100% of the dark matter, so the open questions are mixed cold-plus-warm scenarios (a sterile fraction below 1, constrained in 0812.0010 and 2504.06367), resonant production, and DW contributions on top of other production channels (1512.05369). Warning: no sterile-neutrino production-fraction tool was available in this toolset, so those fractions still need to be computed.

result.summary:
Pure DW sterile neutrinos at 20 keV cannot be all of the dark matter under this tool's physics: the tool's own X-ray check (NuSTAR M31, Roach+ 2020) excludes the f_s = 1 point. At 29 and 45 keV the tool cannot decide either way, because it has no X-ray limit near those masses; the 'not excluded' flag there means no coverage, not allowed. The success criteria are only partly met. The f_s = 1 mixings and the plot are done, but the X-ray limit on sin^2 2theta and f_s at that limit are missing: the tool returns only an excluded/not-excluded flag from sparse tabulated points, never a numerical limit (finding f-002, question q-06). It assumes pure Dodelson-Widrow (DW) production, with Shi-Fuller resonant production as a separate option (this answers q-01). It reports Omega_s h^2, Delta N_eff, lifetime and free-streaming length, but not f_s directly and not k_hm (finding f-001).

Check at the 3.5 keV line point (7.1 keV, sin^2 2theta = 7e-11): Omega_s h^2 = 0.033, so f_s = 0.275 (tc-...-23).

Omega_s h^2 scales linearly with sin^2 2theta, which the 374-point grid confirms. At sin^2 2theta = 1e-12 the tool gives Omega_s h^2 = 0.003041 (20 keV), 0.00361 (22 keV), 0.005936 (29 keV) and 0.01309 (45 keV) (tc-...-31). Scaling to Omega_s h^2 = 0.12 gives the mixing for f_s = 1. This rescaling is my own arithmetic, not a direct tool output.

| m_s | sin^2 2theta at f_s = 1 | Tool X-ray check at that mixing |
|---|---|---|
| 20 keV | 3.95e-11 | Excluded by NuSTAR M31 (tc-...-33) |
| 22 keV | 3.32e-11 | Not run |
| 29 keV | 2.02e-11 | No tabulated limit within 30% in mass, so undecided (tc-...-35) |
| 45 keV | 9.17e-12 | No tabulated limit within 30% in mass, so undecided (tc-...-34) |
| 7.1 keV | 2.55e-10 | Not run (scaled from the same grid) |

Because there are no numerical X-ray limits, I cannot give f_s at the maximal X-ray-allowed mixing, or the fraction that remains allowed, at the four Lyman-alpha floors. This needs d-04's numerical limits: f_s,max = sin^2 2theta_X / sin^2 2theta(f_s=1).

BBN does not matter here. A 6400-point DW scan over 1-100 keV and sin^2 2theta = 1e-14 to 1e-6 found 3092 overclosing points and 968 BBN-excluded points. The largest BBN-allowed mixing is about 3e-8 near 26 keV and 1.5e-8 near 50 keV, roughly 3 orders of magnitude above the f_s = 1 line (f-003).

result.summary: Thermal-relic limits checked (f-005, tc-...-36/45/46/47). 2309.04533 (checked against the full text): m_WDM > 5.7 keV (95% CL) from HIRES+UVES at z = 4.2-5.0 with k_max = 0.2 s/km; restricting to k_max < 0.1 s/km with earlier thermal-history priors gives 4.1 keV. Its main small-scale systematics are IGM peculiar velocities and inhomogeneous reionization, and it says the thermal-history uncertainty now matters less. The other three were checked against their arXiv abstracts only, not the full texts: 2209.14220 gives > 3.1 keV with a likelihood peak at 4.5 keV (4.0 < z < 5.2, Boera+2019 data, suppression saturates at k > 0.1 s/km); 1306.2314 gives > 3.3 keV from 25 z > 4 HIRES/MIKE quasars; 1702.01764 gives XQ-100 1.4 keV, HIRES/MIKE 4.1 keV and combined 5.3 keV assuming a power-law T(z), or 3.5 keV if temperature jumps of 5000 K are allowed. Mixed-DM bounds (f-006): 2504.06367 gives f_WDM < 0.16, 0.35, 0.50, 0.67 (2 sigma) at thermal-relic masses 1, 2, 3, 4 keV (so these are thermal-relic bounds, answering q-02). 0812.0010 is expressed directly in the non-resonant (DW) sterile mass: pure-WDM limits are m_nrp >= 8 keV (99.7%) and 12.1 keV (Bayesian 95%), and any mass above 5 keV is allowed if F_wdm < 0.6 (99.7%) or F_wdm < 0.35 (Bayesian 95%). The 2504.06367 masses mapped to DW masses of about 4.4, 11, 18 and 28 keV are my own estimate from the unverified Viel 2005 formula, not a tool result. result.summary: Two of the three success criteria are not met: there is no table under a second mapping, so no spread between mappings, and the DW <p/T> check was not done. What was established: (1) The Viel et al. 2005 relation is checked against the full text (f-010; source text at /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-lyman-wdm/runs/261019_110120/astro-ph_0501562.txt). Eq. (5) reads m_sterile = 4.43 keV (m_thermal/1 keV)^{4/3} (0.25(0.7)^2/omega_x)^{1/3}, which confirms the coefficient 4.43 keV and the exponents 4/3 and -1/3. The paper gets it by equating omega_x and m_x/T_x, treating the DW spectrum as a rescaled Fermi-Dirac distribution, so the thermal and DW transfer functions are identical by construction. (2) Its fitting form is T(k) = [1+(alpha k)^{2nu}]^{-5/nu} with nu = 1.12, fitted for k < 5 h/Mpc. For thermal relics alpha = 0.049 (m_x/keV)^{-1.11} (Omega_x/0.25)^{0.11} (h/0.7)^{1.22} h^-1 Mpc. By my own arithmetic k_hm = 0.325/alpha, which gives about 23.3, 25.0, 31.8 and 45.8 h/Mpc for 3.1, 3.3, 4.1 and 5.7 keV. These lie outside the k range the fit was calibrated on, and DW k_hm is identical under this mapping (f-011). (3) My own arithmetic gives DW floors, under Viel with omega_dm = 0.12, of 20.2, 21.9, 29.3 and 45.4 keV; with omega = 0.1225 they are 20.0, 21.8, 29.1 and 45.1 keV (f-012). (4) The framework in 2007.13751 is T(k) = [1+(alpha k)^beta]^gamma. It reduces to the Viel form when beta = 2nu and gamma = -5/nu, and a 2 keV WDM is fitted by [0.02, 2.2, -4.5]. In the sections read it gives no DW-specific relation (f-013). Which mapping to use with d-01: Viel Eq. (5), because it is the convention behind the board's floors. This is a provisional recommendation: other mappings may shift the floors, but no second mapping has been checked. Not done: a second mapping (Abazajian astro-ph/0512631 was downloaded to the run directory but not read; the Bozek/Murgia half-mode relations were not found), the spread between mappings, the DW <p/T> of about 3.15 T_nu, the comparison with the tool's free-streaming length, and cite() entries in references.bib. See dead end x-03 and question q-08.

result.summary: Half the success criteria are met: the literature statements on whether pure Dodelson-Widrow (DW) production can be all of the dark matter are quote-verified, but the numerical table of X-ray limits on sin^2 2theta could not be built. (1) Literature statements, all quote-verified. Merle 2017 (arXiv:1702.08430) says DW production is 'nowadays known to be excluded by observations'; that rests on structure formation together with X-ray bounds (f-007). This statement rests on structure formation combined with X-ray bounds; the review does not make an X-ray-only exclusion claim.

Roach et al. 2022 (arXiv:2207.04572, NuSTAR Milky Way halo, about 7 Ms/detector blank-sky plus about 20 Ms/detector stacked data) find no anomalous lines and set sin^2(2theta) limits for m_s = 6-40 keV. Quote: "we strongly disfavor a ~7-keV sterile neutrino decaying into a 3.5-keV photon" and "we derive leading limits on sterile neutrinos with masses ~15–18 keV and ~25–40 keV, reaching or extending below the big bang nucleosynthesis limit". The conclusions add that the parameter space "is now mostly covered", but this "does not fully rule out sterile neutrinos as the only DM component"; it shows "the simple and elegant mixing production mechanism [8, 9] may be insufficient". The authors therefore do NOT claim that X-ray data alone exclude 100% DW dark matter. Their "mostly covered" statement relies on adding satellite-counting bounds.

Roach et al. 2020 (arXiv:1908.09037, NuSTAR Galactic bulge, about 190 ks) give 95% one-sided limits on the decay rate Gamma for m_s = 10-40 keV, quoted in Gamma [s^-1] rather than sin^2 2theta. Their Fig. 5 plots these limits on a Gamma axis spanning 1e-29 to 1e-27 s^-1, compared with Neronov+2016, Perez+2017 and Ng+2019. The paper states the limits are "comparable to previous NuSTAR limits" and improve on earlier ones by about 2x at 10-12 keV. findings.claim: Combined table of allowed DW fraction versus mass (Lyman-alpha side). At 7.1 keV: 0812.0010 gives F_wdm < 0.35 (quote-verified, d-02), and 2504.06367 mapped to DW mass gives f between 0.16 and 0.35 (my estimate; the mapped points are 4.4 and 11 keV). It is also below the 0812.0010 pure-DW floor of 12.1 keV, so the binding constraint is Lyman-alpha mixed-DM, f_s <~ 0.2-0.35. At 20 and 22 keV: 2504.06367 mapped gives f <~ 0.5-0.67 (mapped points 18 and 28 keV), and 20/22 keV are below the 29 keV (4.1 keV variant) and 45 keV (5.7 keV variant) Viel-mapped pure-DW floors. The tool's X-ray check excludes f_s = 1 at 20 keV, so the binding constraint is Lyman-alpha (f <~ 0.5-0.67) unless a numerical X-ray limit is stricter. At 29 keV: f = 1 is allowed by Lyman-alpha only for the 4.1 keV variant (floor ~29 keV, unverified Viel mapping), while for the 5.7 keV variant f <~ 0.67 or more. At 45 keV: f = 1 is allowed by Lyman-alpha even for the 5.7 keV variant (floor ~45 keV). At 29 and 45 keV, X-ray limits are presumably binding, but no numerical X-ray limit is available, so f_s,max(X-ray) stays undetermined.

issues.text: The tool's DW normalisation has not been cross-checked. The common Abazajian-type fit, Omega h^2 ~ 0.1 (sin^2 2theta / 3e-9)(m_s / 3 keV)^1.8, gives sin^2 2theta(f_s=1) of about 7-8e-10 at 7.1 keV. The tool's value is 2.55e-10, roughly a factor of 3 lower. DW abundance predictions differ by factors of a few in the literature (hadronic uncertainties, Asaka-Laine-Shaposhnikov). Any f_s,max derived from this line inherits that factor and must state the source of the normalisation.

The tc-...-31 excerpt shows only the 7.1 keV row. The 20, 22, 29 and 45 keV Omega_s h^2 values are not visible in the quoted evidence, although the arithmetic from them is internally consistent (0.12/0.003041 x 1e-12 = 3.95e-11, and so on). The full rows from sterile_nu_grid_DW_a74034.csv should be quoted.

The counts (968 BBN-excluded, 3092 overclosing) appear in the evidence. The maxima of the BBN-allowed mixing (3.03e-8 at 26.2 keV, 1.5e-8 at 49.7 keV) do not. Those mixings lie deep in the overclosed region, so 'BBN does not constrain DW DM' is correct but trivially so. The claim should say this.

The Merle quote attributes the DW exclusion to the hot-like momentum spectrum, which is a structure-formation argument. The finding's addition that the statement 'rests on structure formation combined with X-ray bounds' is an interpretation, not part of the quote. It should be labelled as such.

contested.reason: The only excerpt (tc-261019_1-w2-d-04-82, chars 30000-44000) covers GRXE abundance fitting. It contains none of the claimed content: no Gamma limits, no Fig. 5 axis range of 1e-29 to 1e-27 s^-1, no 'about 2x better at 10-12 keV' statement and no weakening near 16 or 30-40 keV. The claim may be true, but the quoted evidence does not show it.

The half-mode convention is non-standard. The usual definition (Schneider et al. 2012, used by Viel 2013 and Irsic 2023) places k_hm where T(k) = 1/2, i.e. T^2 = 1/4, not T^2 = 1/2. With nu = 1.12 that gives k_hm = (2^{nu/5}-1)^{1/(2nu)}/alpha, about 0.45/alpha instead of 0.325/alpha, so roughly 32, 35, 44 and 63 h/Mpc rather than 23-46 h/Mpc. The alpha arithmetic checks out, but the excerpt (tc-261019_1-w2-d-03-74) shows neither the fitting formula nor nu = 1.12.

The tool-side values are supported: the CSV shows 0.000471462 and 0.00304114, and the rescaling is correct. The published-formula side is not shown. Neither excerpt (tc-261019_1-w2-d-05-85, tc-261019_1-w2-d-05-88) contains Abazajian 2006 Eq. 7 or the ALS coefficients (-7.6195, -1.7428), and cite() was not run. The ALS fit is applied far above its stated M <= 4 keV validity. The 3-16x discrepancy is plausible but unverified.

It depends entirely on the unverified published normalisations in f-014. Its statement that the X-ray exclusion at 20 keV gets stronger rests on f-002, which is itself contested. The arithmetic and the logical direction are correct, but the evidence chain is incomplete.

The 2504.06367 and 0812.0010 excerpts are title pages only and contain no fraction bounds. Mapping thermal-relic mixed-DM bounds onto DW masses with the pure-WDM Viel relation is an untested extrapolation. X-ray exclusion of f_s = 1 says nothing about whether f ~ 0.5-0.67 is X-ray allowed. For fractional DW the line flux scales as f_s * sin^2 2theta, which is proportional to f_s^2, and this scaling was not used. The 'unverified Viel' label is outdated now that f-010 exists.
